input: Minced rather than intact beef in the tested older-adult meal
biological_role: The tested texture change increased six-hour appearance of dietary phenylalanine in ten older men.
evidence_limitation: Single crossover with 135 g intrinsically labelled beef. Total plasma EAA concentrations and muscle protein synthesis did not differ detectably. Not a universal meat, protein or neurotransmitter prescription; earlier no-selected-SOP wording records the prior assessment.
reader_description: The tested texture change increased six-hour appearance of dietary phenylalanine in ten older men.

biological_role: The tested formulation changed presynaptic structural markers in rats.
evidence_limitation: Puncta are markers, not ultrastructurally verified contact counts. Formulation- and region-specific animal evidence does not establish that ordinary magnesium foods increase human synapses or improve ADHD.
reader_description: The tested formulation changed presynaptic structural markers in rats.

input: Tested fibre/fruit-rich mixed meal versus the high-fat/high-carbohydrate comparison
biological_role: The meal comparison measured different acute mononuclear NF-kB DNA-binding responses.
evidence_limitation: Small parallel-group acute comparison; multiple ingredients and macronutrients differed. No isolated fibre, fruit or constituent effect; LAL/LBP are not direct proof of gut leakage, portal origin, LPS bioactivity or brain benefit. CRP and TNF-alpha did not change.
reader_description: The meal comparison measured different acute mononuclear NF-kB DNA-binding responses.

biological_role: The tested 24-week exposure increased muscle carnitine and changed exercise-dependent fuel handling.
evidence_limitation: Lipid use is partly inferred from glycogen sparing; CPT transport flux was not directly measured. Large carbohydrate co-exposure and extracted formulation are not meat/dairy effects or a routine dietary recommendation.
reader_description: The tested 24-week exposure increased muscle carnitine and changed exercise-dependent fuel handling.

input: Four-day ketogenic liquid formula in the studied healthy-adult experiment
biological_role: The defined formula raised tracer/model-estimated cerebral acetoacetate metabolism.
evidence_limitation: Small short-term nonrandomised study; PET metabolic rates are tracer/model estimates, not direct neuronal oxidation measurements. Combined total ketone energy contribution was estimated separately. No ADHD efficacy or endorsement of routine ketogenic dieting.
reader_description: The defined formula raised tracer/model-estimated cerebral acetoacetate metabolism.

input: Combined progressive exercise as studied in men with type 2 diabetes
biological_role: The programme improved the clamp-associated respiratory-exchange flexibility index in the diabetes group.
evidence_limitation: No inactive randomised comparator; whole-body RER is an index of substrate switching, not a brain-specific assay. The flexibility change was not significant in healthy controls.
reader_description: The programme improved the clamp-associated respiratory-exchange flexibility index in the diabetes group.

input: Low-volume interval cycling in the tested two-week protocol
biological_role: The studied training increased muscle mitochondrial enzyme/protein and TFAM markers.
evidence_limitation: No inactive control, small male sample. These are mitochondrial-content and regulatory markers, not direct counting of newly formed brain mitochondria. Total PGC-1alpha was unchanged.
reader_description: The studied training increased muscle mitochondrial enzyme/protein and TFAM markers.

input: Conditional oral arginine supplementation in the tested type-2-diabetes protocol
biological_role: The studied 9 g/day exposure improved clamp-measured glucose disposal in a small clinical comparison.
evidence_limitation: Incomplete normalisation; small selected clinical population. cGMP change does not isolate causal NO mediation. The 9 g/day supplement protocol is not equivalent to arginine-containing food.
reader_description: The studied 9 g/day exposure improved clamp-measured glucose disposal in a small clinical comparison.

input: Aerobic conditioning in the tested twelve-week programme
biological_role: The randomised training comparison increased high-frequency RR variability, with sex-dependent autonomic effects.
evidence_limitation: Sex-dependent findings, respiration/context-sensitive cardiac proxy, not direct whole-body vagal traffic or universal recovery improvement.
reader_description: The randomised training comparison increased high-frequency RR variability, with sex-dependent autonomic effects.
